p: Weekends and school holidays bring the crowds to Rushden Lakes, especially on sunny days, so arriving early gives you the best choice of parking and a quieter wander around the lake. If you're planning to eat at one of the waterside restaurants at a popular time, booking ahead is wise. Bring binoculars if you've got birdwatchers in the family, and a picnic blanket if you fancy a spot by the water.

Dog walkers are welcome on the wetland paths, though it's worth keeping dogs on leads near nesting birds and around the busier parts of the site. If the weather turns, the shops and cinema give you an easy indoor backup, and it's a handy place to meet up with friends or family from across Northamptonshire and Bedfordshire.

The surrounding Nene Valley is packed with green spaces. Stanwick Lakes, a few miles up the A45, is a large countryside site with walking and cycling trails, play areas and a visitor centre, making it a lovely addition for an outdoorsy family. Higham Ferrers, right next door to Rushden, is a pretty market town with a historic church and the remains of a medieval college. Further afield, Wellingborough and Northampton offer more shopping and attractions, while the Nene Way footpath follows the river through the countryside for keen walkers. Between the lakes and the shops, there's enough here to fill a whole day. Pack wellies if it's been wet, as some of the paths near the water can get muddy after rain.
